import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Green's Open Problem 15

References:
- [Gr24] [Green, Ben. "100 open problems." (2024).](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.15)
- [BJP14] T. Brown, V. Jungić and A. Poelstra, "On double 3-term arithmetic progressions",
  Integers 14 (2014), Paper No. A43.
- [CCS14] J. Cassaigne, J. D. Currie, L. Schaeffer and J. Shallit, "Avoidance of additive cubes and
  related results", Adv. in Appl. Math. 56 (2014), 25–66.
-/

open Set
open scoped NNReal

namespace Green15

/--
Does there exist a Lipschitz function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Z}$ whose graph
$\Gamma = \{(n, f(n)) : n \in \mathbb{N}\} \subseteq \mathbb{Z}^2$ is free of 3-term progressions?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 11]
theorem green_15 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ K : ℝ≥0, ∃ f : ℕ → ℤ, LipschitzWith K f ∧
      IsAPOfLengthFree {((n, f n) : ℤ × ℤ) | (n : ℕ)} 3 := by
  sorry

/--
The answer is YES for 4-term progressions [BJP14].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem green_15_ap4 :
    ∃ K : ℝ≥0, ∃ f : ℕ → ℤ, LipschitzWith K f ∧
      IsAPOfLengthFree  {((n, f n) : ℤ × ℤ) | (n : ℕ)} 4 := by
  sorry

-- TODO(jeangud) Add finitary version

end Green15

findings.description: The module bibliography's [CCS14] entry (lines 26–27) gives the wrong title and publication details for the Cassaigne–Currie–Schaeffer–Shallit paper underlying the 4-term result: it lists “Avoidance of additive cubes and related results”, Adv. in Appl. Math. 56 (2014), 25–66. The intended paper is “Avoiding three consecutive blocks of the same size and same sum”, J. ACM 61 (2014), no. 2, Article 10. This is a reference error, not a defect in either theorem statement.
findings.source_evidence: Green's bibliography, reference [65], identifies the paper as “Avoiding three consecutive blocks of the same size and same sum. J. ACM 61 (2014), no. 2, Art. 10, 17 pp.” (https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf). The title is confirmed by the primary source https://arxiv.org/abs/1106.5204, and the publication details by Shallit's 2014 publication list at https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/~shallit/papers.html. Brown–Jungić–Poelstra also cites this same paper as reference [4].
findings.suggested_fix: Replace [CCS14] with: J. Cassaigne, J. D. Currie, L. Schaeffer and J. Shallit, “Avoiding three consecutive blocks of the same size and same sum”, J. ACM 61 (2014), no. 2, Article 10, 17 pp.; optionally link https://arxiv.org/abs/1106.5204.

reformulations.difference: The cited [BJP14] passage states existence of an increasing sequence of positive integers with bounded gaps and no double 4-term arithmetic progression. Lean instead permits any integer-valued Lipschitz function and requires its graph in ℤ² to be 4-term-progression-free.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A double progression is precisely a nontrivial progression in the sequence's graph. Conversely, given a K-Lipschitz f, choose an integer C > K and set g(n) = f(n) + Cn - f(0) + 1. Then g(0) = 1 and its successive gaps lie between C-K > 0 and C+K, so g is positive, strictly increasing, and has bounded gaps. The affine bijection (x,y) ↦ (x,y+Cx-f(0)+1) preserves progressions and maps the graph of f to that of g. In the other direction, bounded gaps in an increasing sequence imply the Lipschitz bound by telescoping. Reindexing between zero-based and one-based sequences preserves all these properties. Thus the existence statements are equivalent; citing [BJP14] for this result is valid.

review.notes:
Both theorem statements are mathematically faithful. The currently served Green list still poses the 3-term question as open and explicitly records the affirmative 4-term result. The source's graph comprehension says n ∈ ℤ despite declaring f : ℕ → ℤ; Lean's natural-number indexing follows that declared domain and the cited one-sided sequence formulations.

/workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles successfully. Its sorry-free checks establish that every such graph is infinite, constant graphs fail both progression-free conditions, K = 0 cannot witness either statement, and global Lipschitz continuity is equivalent to uniformly bounded consecutive differences. Finite computation of the cited morphism also found no 4-term progression in the sampled partial-sum graph. The reviewed file remains byte-for-byte identical to the committed file.

Green's ancillary link to Erdős Problem 193 returned a Cloudflare challenge despite a descriptive User-Agent; neither declaration depended on that page for verification.
